Accept Jotun ceasefire.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Mitwold, the motion agreed a ceasefire running from the start of the Spring Equinox 377YE until the start of the Spring Equinox 379YE. Imperial armies were barred from entering territories claimed by the Jotun, including Liathaven and Mournwold, while Jotun campaign armies would not enter Imperial territory. Subsidiary motions to outlaw raiding on the Jotun during the ceasefire and to declare them foreigners for its duration were defeated. At the Spring Equinox 378YE the Senate extended the treaty to the start of the Spring Equinox 380YE, but at the Summer Solstice 379YE it abrogated the ceasefire early in order to give military aid to the Lasambrian orcs against the Jotun.

n.Jotun: The Jotun's offer of peace was accepted, so their campaign armies would stay out of Imperial territory while their claimed lands were spared Imperial attack, until the Senate broke the truce in Summer 379YE to aid the Lasambrian orcs against them.

t.Liathaven: As a territory claimed by the Jotun, Liathaven was closed to Imperial armies for the duration of the ceasefire, leaving it in Jotun hands without Imperial challenge.
t.Mournwold: The ceasefire barred Imperial armies from entering Jotun-held Mournwold, halting any Imperial campaign to retake it while the truce held.

Archive:377YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.d: Several Senate seats changed hands. Lady Adia took Weirwater and Gideon took Bastion. In Hercynia, Rhain replaced Cei Windstrider, whom the Navarr National Assembly had revoked. Hector kept Zenith after being revoked by the Synod and re-elected. New generals included Estana, Skayde, Richard Talbot, Tanwyn Ankarien, Olaf Gregorson and Vahne, and Septima of Shatterspire became Warmage. In the Synod, Jared, Epaph and Agnetha De Rondell became Cardinals of Loyalty, Pride and Wisdom, and six Archmagi were declared. White Granite Bourse seats were not re-elected because of concerns over economic stability in a time of crisis. Seats in Druj- and Thule-held lands were withheld from auction.

n.Dawn: Lady Adia of House Arwood claimed Weirwater's Senate seat from Marek, and Skayde replaced Eryk Rykker as general of the Golden Sun. Agnetha De Rondell became Cardinal of Wisdom and Maurice de Gauvain was declared Archmage of Autumn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj held the Great Forest at Reikos and the Great Pits of Ennerlund, which would not be auctioned until those lands were Imperial again.
n.Highguard: Gideon claimed Bastion's seat from Simiel of the Shattered Tower, and Ruth kept command of the Granite Pillar. Highguard dominated the Synod, with Jared and Epaph appointed Cardinals of Loyalty and Pride and Lazarus remaining Cardinal of Courage.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Martok was listed as replacing Klor of the Winter Sun, pending confirmation, while Braka kept the Summer Storm. Gralka remained Conscience of the Senate and Bruk held the Steel Fist.
n.Navarr: The Navarr National Assembly revoked Cei Windstrider in his absence, and Rhain replaced him as senator for Hercynia; Rhys claimed Miaren from Bledri Eternal. Hywel Summercrow became Gatekeeper of Wisdom and Meir Pathfinder was Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield.
n.The Brass Coast: Sallur kept Feroz's seat, and Estana replaced Yasmina as general of the Red Wind Corsairs. Yasmina was listed as taking the Fire of the South from Deigo, pending confirmation.
n.The League: Mirislav kept Sarvos and League clergy held three Cardinalates: Ambition, Prosperity and The Way. League merchants held many Imperial Bourse seats, along with the Regario Dossier and the Mint.
n.The Marches: Richard Talbot replaced Bjorn as general of the Drakes. Friar Alan Young remained Gatekeeper of Loyalty and William Bolholt was Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule held the Brilliant Shore, which would not be auctioned until Skarsind was Imperial again.
n.Urizen: Hector kept Zenith despite his Spring revocation and could not be revoked again before the next normal election, while Probus kept Redoubt. Tanwyn Ankarien replaced Decius Cascade at the Citadel Guard and Cyrus Cascade became Gatekeeper of Courage.
n.Varushka: Constantin kept Karov, and Olaf Gregorson Strascovichlaf replaced Zakhar 'the grim' as general of the Northern Eagle. Petra Petrivna Melikov remained Cardinal of Vigilance and Simargl was appointed Dean of the Lyceum.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark National Assembly revoked General Merrick in his absence, and Vahne replaced him at the Green Shield. Atte kept Sermersuaq, Erkenbrand kept the Fist of the Mountain and Wyrda Bjornadottir was Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern.

Construct Otkodov spy network.d: The motion passed at 12 Thrones with no votes against, and the funds went to Morrow. Ioseph, Senator for Morrow, paid the 10 weirwood during the Summer Solstice downtime. The network carries an upkeep of 2 Thrones a season from the Senate budget and takes three months to build. Because a territory map of Otkodov had already been found, the network was to target Verthandi. Once complete, any Imperial citizen may assign military units to it. Five units would reveal a map of Verthandi's settlements, ten its armies, naval routes and trading partners, and fifteen its fortifications. Not all Imperial citizens know the network exists.

n.Thule: The Thule territories of Otkodov and Verthandi became targets of covert Imperial intelligence. The network was meant to expose Verthandi's settlements, armies, trade and fortifications.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Senator for Morrow proposed the motion, received the funds and paid the 10 weirwood to build the network.

t.Morrow: Morrow's senator Ioseph proposed the motion and paid for it, and the Senate's money was distributed to Morrow.
t.Otkodov: The Empire was to build a secret spy network in Thule-held Otkodov over three months. Otkodov's own territory map had already been discovered.
t.Verthandi: Verthandi, the central Thule territory, was the network's intelligence target. Depending on how many military units are assigned, its settlements, armies, naval routes, trading partners and fortifications could be revealed.

Fortify Skogei.d: Proposed by Hahnmark and seconded by Therunin, the Summer 377YE motion funded reinforcement of the foothold in Skarsind on the military council's recommendation. It passed at 15 Thrones, with the money going to Hahnmark. In Autumn 377YE a Hahnmark motion seconded by Kallavesa, to maintain and upgrade the fortifications in Skarsind, passed unanimously. The work cost 88 wains of white granite, took four seasons and carries an upkeep of 10 Thrones. Hengest Dun, Senator for Hahnmark, presented all the granite in four instalments between Summer 377YE and Summer 378YE. The finished fortification at Skogei is the Will of the Wintermark, called Hengesthal.

n.Thule: The fortification was built in Skarsind, a Thule-held territory, strengthening the Empire's foothold against Thule control there.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Senator for Hahnmark, Hengest Dun, drove the project and supplied all 88 wains of granite. The completed fortress bears the nation's name as the Will of the Wintermark, or Hengesthal.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's senator proposed both motions and received the Senate funds. Hengest Dun then personally presented every wain of white granite needed for construction.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind gained a new fortification at Skogei to hold the Imperial foothold established there. It was completed as the Will of the Wintermark.

r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: Skogei became the site of Hengesthal, the Will of the Wintermark, a granite fortification raised over four seasons to secure the Imperial foothold.

Permit dredging of Feverwater.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Miaren, the motion authorised an attempt to dredge the Feverwater. The cost was hard to estimate but put at more than ten wains of weirwood; Merel of the Pathfinders of Therunin later paid thirteen wains after the Spring Equinox. The civil service warned that the lake is home to swamp monsters likely to kill many who try, and noted that no magical netting techniques are known, the Brass Coast using ordinary nets on the Scorrero. Once complete, the dredging yielded a modest four measures of crafting materials each season. The position was treated as a Navarr national appointment, voted on by Navarr senators.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the civil service mused that the apparent madness of the venture might lead Druj forces active in the area to underestimate the Empire in some unpredictable way.
n.Navarr: A Navarr pathfinder, Merel, was granted the right to dredge the Feverwater and paid thirteen wains of weirwood for it, and the resulting position became a Navarr national appointment chosen by Navarr senators.

t.Therunin: Therunin's senator proposed the dredging of the Feverwater, a monster-haunted lake partly within the territory, which went on to produce four measures of crafting materials each season.
